newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: NAMIBIA CABINET APPROVES FISHING RIGHTS, SEAL QUOTA.
newsitem.headline: NAMIBIA CABINET APPROVES FISHING RIGHTS, SEAL QUOTA.

text.p: The Namibian cabinet has approved long-term fishing rights for 1998 and seal quotas for the 1997 season.
Briefing journalists on the cabinet decisions on Wednesday, Information and Broadcasting Deputy Minister Ignatius Shixwameni said a total of 138 four-, seven- and 10-year rights had been approved.

These are: demersal hake 36, demersal monk 11, linefish (larger vessels) 9, horse mackerel 12, pelagic 28, rock lobster 18, red crab three, seals two, tuna (pole & line) 15 and tuna (sashimi longline) four.

From September, the Ministry of Fisheries and Marine resources will invite applications for four-year rights to fishing in demersal hake, horse mackerel, pelagic, rock lobster, red crab, seals and tuna (sashimi longline), which expire on December 31, 1997.
The cabinet has also approved a seal harvesting quota of 26,000 pups and 4,000 bulls with a maximum length of 1,7 metres to protect the stock of breeding bulls.
The 1997 season commenced on August 6 and ends November 15.

As in the past observers of the Wildlife Society will be allowed access to the harvests to comment and recommend improvements to the two concessionaires Sea Lion Products (Pty) Ltd and Namibia Venison and Marine Products (Pty) Ltd.
